report.summary: Chunk 2 of 4 of daedalus/eval/report.py: defines render_tier1 and render_arms functions, building report lines for tier1 and arms A/B/C evaluations.
risks: render_arms | medium | 'by_provenance' aggregation keys used before definition; if result dict lacks expected structure, KeyError may occur. | Check that 'by_provenance' is populated with nested dicts containing 'n_tasks', 'mean_recall_A', etc. before calling render_arms.
render_arms | medium | 'focus_withheld' key accessed but not defined in result; missing key may cause KeyError. | Verify that result dict includes 'focus_withheld' key or use .get().

handoff.purpose: Define render_tier1 and render_arms functions to generate report strings for tier1 and arms evaluations.

symbols.name: render_tier1
symbols.note: Takes a result dict and returns a formatted report string for tier1 evaluation.

symbols.name: render_arms
symbols.note: Takes a result dict and returns a formatted report string for arms A/B/C evaluation.

claims.text: Healthy (non-errored, non-focus-withheld) misses only -- an errored task has no 'missed' list at all (it never got as far as measuring recall); a focus-withheld task has none either (the fence refused before recall was ever measured). Both are reported in their own unmissable sections, not folded in here as a miss.
claims.why: The claim describes behavior of errored and focus-withheld tasks that is not verifiable from this chunk alone; it references other sections and external logic.

claims.text: ERORRED section -- a per-task resolution failure (bad repo label, or a target no longer in the index -- e.g. a quarantined mint task whose file moved) is EXCLUDED from every mean above but must never go unreported: 'a degraded measurement is reported, never silent.'
claims.why: The claim about exclusion from means and reporting policy cannot be fully verified from this chunk alone; it refers to code outside the chunk.

claims.text: Absent entirely (result.get, not result[...]) for any pre-existing caller that hand-built a Tier-1 result dict without this key -- and always absent when there are zero errored tasks, so this block adds NO lines to that report.
claims.why: The code uses result.get('errored') or [], which matches the claim about safe access and absence when zero errored tasks.

claims.text: A/B/C: distilled slice vs whole-repo concat vs BM25 retrieval. Model-free (recall via substring match, no LLM), so this runs offline every time.
claims.why: The claim about model-free recall via substring match and offline execution cannot be verified from this chunk; it refers to external logic.

claims.text: Errored rows carry no recall_A/tokens_A/... at all (see harness._task_error_row) -- they are reported in their own section below, not in this table. FOCUS-WITHHELD rows (harness._focus_withheld_row) are excluded the same way, into their own section.
claims.why: The claim references harness._task_error_row and harness._focus_withheld_row, which are outside this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: B = naive whole-repo concat. R_B/TOK_B are measured against the TRUE, FULL, UNTRUNCATED repo text -- beating a truncated B is not a win. B_TRUNC@CAP = yes means: if this task ran Tier 2, B would be cut down to fit the model's context window -- a WEAKER baseline than the R_B/TOK_B shown here.
claims.why: The claim about measurement against true full repo text and Tier 2 context window cannot be verified from this chunk; refers to external logic.

claims.text: C = BM25 (k1=1.2, b=0.75) top-k retrieval, budgeted to the SAME token count as A. The 'dumb retrieval' baseline that matters commercially.
claims.why: The claim about BM25 parameters and budget cannot be verified from this chunk; refers to external implementation.

observations.what: render_tier1 uses result['per_task'] and result['by_provenance'] without checking existence; if result lacks these keys, KeyError will be raised.
observations.where: render_tier1, lines iterating per_task and calling _provenance_breakdown_lines

observations.what: render_arms accesses result['by_provenance'][prov][tier] with nested dict keys; if result['by_provenance'] is missing or has unexpected structure, KeyError may occur.
Both functions use helper functions _pct, _table, _provenance_breakdown_lines, _focus_withheld_lines which are not defined in this chunk; their behavior is unchecked.
observations.where: render_tier1 and render_arms, calls to helper functions

observations.what: In render_arms, the variable 'by_provenance' is accessed but not defined; it should be result['by_provenance'].
